notes.meaning: Temple officers arrived at the public prison expecting to find the apostles locked inside. Instead, the cells were completely empty. The officers had to return to the Jewish high council with nothing to show for their trip.

The officers reported that the jail remained locked tight and the guards were still standing watch outside the doors. Yet when they unlocked and entered the room, no one was there. This made it clear that God had freed the apostles without disturbing the locks or the guards.

The captain in charge of the temple police and the leading priests were deeply puzzled by the report. They could not understand how the prisoners had escaped or where this strange situation would lead. Their attempts to silence the movement were quickly unraveling.

A messenger suddenly arrived with shocking news for the council. The very men who had been locked up were standing openly in the temple courts, teaching the crowds about Jesus. They had not run away into hiding, but went straight back to doing what God had told them to do.

The temple captain and his men went to bring the apostles back, but they treated them gently and used no force. They were terrified that the listening crowd might turn on them and stone them to death. The apostles agreed peacefully to go along rather than cause a public riot.

The officers brought the apostles into the council chamber to face the Sanhedrin, the highest Jewish ruling court. The high priest immediately stepped forward to lead the questioning. This gave the apostles another public moment to speak for Christ.

The high priest reminded the apostles that the council had strictly forbidden them to teach about Jesus. He complained that their message had spread all over Jerusalem, making the leaders look guilty of murdering Him. The leaders could not bear hearing the truth about what they had done to Jesus.

Peter and the other apostles replied that their highest duty was to obey God rather than any human ruler. When the commands of earthly authorities go against what God directs, believers must always follow God. The apostles were not rebelling for personal gain, but standing firm on God's call.

Peter explained that the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob had raised Jesus back to life. In sharp contrast, the council members were the ones who put Him to death by hanging Him on a wooden cross. The apostles showed that they served the true God of Israel, while the leaders had rejected His Messiah.

God raised Jesus up to the place of highest honor at His right hand as King and Savior. He did this so people in Israel could turn from their sins and receive full forgiveness. Jesus offers true spiritual rescue, beginning with a changed heart.

The apostles testified that they saw Jesus alive with their own eyes. The Holy Spirit also proved the truth of their message through miraculous signs and transformed lives. God gives this promised Spirit to all who yield their lives to Him.

differ.view: Obeying God means trusting in Christ for salvation, and the Holy Spirit is given as a seal to everyone who believes.
The Holy Spirit gives more of His gifts and inward strength to believers in proportion to how faithfully they obey His daily guidance.

notes.meaning: Hearing these words cut the council members to the quick with furious anger. Instead of feeling sorrow for their sins, they were so enraged that they wanted to execute the apostles on the spot. Hardened hearts often answer the truth of God with violent hatred.

A Pharisee named Gamaliel, a respected scholar of the law, stood up in the assembly. He had the apostles removed from the room for a few moments so the court could speak privately. God used this wise teacher to calm a deadly situation.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Early Christian tradition suggested that Gamaliel later became a secret believer in Jesus and was eventually baptized by the apostles.

notes.meaning: Gamaliel urged his fellow leaders to pause and think very carefully before taking action. He warned them not to make a hasty decision out of temper that they might later regret. Rash anger in religious matters often leads to grave injustice.

Gamaliel reminded them of an earlier rebel named Theudas, who claimed to be an important leader and drew four hundred men. When Theudas was killed, his movement completely fell apart and vanished. Movements driven purely by human pride do not last long.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars argue that Luke made a historical error here, because the Jewish historian Josephus describes a rebel named Theudas about ten years after this council meeting.

notes.meaning: Next, Gamaliel brought up Judas the Galilean, who led an uprising during the Roman tax census. Judas also died, and his followers were scattered in defeat. Gamaliel used these known events to prove that false uprisings quickly fade away on their own.

Gamaliel advised the council to leave the apostles alone and let them go. He reasoned that if their message was merely an invention of men, it would collapse just like the rebellions before it. Human religious frauds have a very short lifespan.

Gamaliel warned that if this work was truly from God, nothing the council did could stop it. In fact, fighting against the apostles would mean picking a fight with God Himself. True wisdom knows that human power can never defeat God's purposes.

The council was convinced by Gamaliel's advice and dropped the plan to execute the apostles. Still, they had the apostles whipped with lashes to punish them and ordered them never to speak in Jesus' name again. Even when worldly opponents compromise, they often show their cruelty.

The apostles walked away from the council full of joy despite their painful wounds. They considered it a privilege to suffer public shame for the name of Jesus, who had suffered for them. God's grace gave them courage to find honor where the world meant to bring disgrace.

The apostles never stopped sharing the gospel, preaching both publicly in the temple courts and privately in homes every single day. They kept proclaiming the good news that Jesus is the promised Christ. Threats and beatings could not quiet their joyful testimony.
